rites.name: Coraullus
rites.text: Coraullus is a concept of the Jorernaston cycle, drawn during the Seeding when makers plant the Weave and quiet powers sleep. It belongs to the Holy Age, a time of flame, temples and sworn orders that shaped the early world's rites.

rites.name: Tenvameno
rites.text: Tenvameno is a concept in the Walled Age of Jorernaston, the idea that a town's holding walls are kept standing by a shared oath rather than by stone alone. Its orders and churches teach that breaking the oath is the one thing a wall cannot survive. It is most often invoked when first crossings of a river or ridge are being negotiated.

rites.name: Isitheth
rites.text: Isitheth is a concept of Jorernaston, born in the Walled Age as the idea of a holding wall that a whole order swears to keep. Its meaning grew through centuries of temples and first crossings, so that to speak its name in the Holy Age is to call up the flame that guards the gate.

rites.name: Kelenock
rites.text: Kelenock is a grounded, era-six concept: a patient mind that lives in a single vaulted archive where the shelves are arranged by ruin rather than by date. It quietly trades dangerous understanding to anyone who asks the right question, and its catalogue of hidden knowledge is treated by scholars as the most valuable and most feared object in the region.

rites.name: Pelerock
rites.text: Pelerock is a concept-grade hunting spirit of the Grounded realm in Jorernaston, a lean ember-wolf whose pacts are settled in ash rather than blood. It binds its hunters to a single quarry and claims a tithe of warmth from them, leaving those who break faith as cinder-shrouded revenants.

rites.name: Pelornar
rites.text: Pelornar is a hungry grove-mind that lives in the dim hollows of Jorernaston, reaching out through root-tendrils to those who lie awake at night. It grants its hosts a sharpened body and a restless fury, though the thorny heart it plants in their chest slowly crowds out their gentler instincts.

rites.name: Brestoldon
rites.text: Brestoldon is a patient guardian-concept of the Grounded realm, worshipped by the stonewrights who raise the fortresses of Jorernaston's third age. Its influence hardens walls and sharpens the timing of defenders, lending them an unmoving resolve that outlasts any siege.

rites.name: Thodock
rites.text: Thodock is a grounded concept in the Jorernaston cosmos, a faded lamp-spirit whose light was dimmed when its sky-court cast it out. Its chosen keepers carry a quiet ember in their chest that they can release in brief, sorrowful flares.

rites.name: Craden
rites.text: Craden is a concept of the grounded realm in Jorernaston's sixth era, a quiet patron of those who keep watch over the threshold between the living and the spent. It is said to whisper to lantern-bearers who tend forgotten plots and to reward them with small, careful gifts. Its influence is subtle and rarely seen directly.

rites.name: Kelorden
rites.text: Kelorden is a mirror-speaker of the Grounded realm's sixth age, whose presence makes travelers see the true lines of their own faces in any reflective surface. Its gift is a slow, sustained pressure that can bend a person's self-image, rarely more than a few hundred joules of felt weight at a time.

rites.name: Kelanorath
rites.text: Kelanorath is a concept of patient keeping, a presence said to gather sunken records and murmuring relics into lightless vaults beneath the deepest brine. Its influence is felt mostly in what goes unspoken and what is quietly kept safe from the surface world.

rites.name: Crernath
rites.text: Crernath is a concept in Jorernaston, a resonant hum said to be the first note a sleeping river sings before dawn. Its scholars teach that every stone and reed carries a sliver of it, tuned to the age of the world. Its gifts are small, patient harmonies that steady what has begun to shake.

rites.name: Fenuresten
rites.text: Fenuresten is a sinuous, crowned sovereign of the Jorernaston courts, whose scaled coils are said to coil around the throne of every regent who swears fealty to her. Her ancient ledgers bind the lineages of the realm, and those she favors receive a fragment of her ceremonial bloodline. She is accounted the first to have turned the rites of precedence into a weapon.

rites.name: Fenedar
rites.text: Fenedar is a concept of the Grounded realm in Jorernaston, a mind of tidal stillness that lives in the hour between two lamps going out. It is said to lend the banked-ember inheritance to those who learn to walk without shadows, though its true shape is never agreed upon among the wardens who record it.

rites.name: Pelornar
rites.text: Pelornar is a storm-bound concept of Jorernaston's Grounded realm, an entity of coiled thunder and riding gales that the warlike sky-clans have long sought to appease. Its heralds are said to carry a fraction of its anger in their veins, able to call sudden squalls across open plains.

rites.name: Feneden
rites.text: Feneden is a concept of measured retribution in the Jorernaston, worshipped as the weighing hand that gives every wrong its proper reckoning. Its followers are wardens who carry its verdicts into the world without malice and without mercy beyond what the scale allows.

rites.name: Halordath
rites.text: Halordath is a concept in the Jorernaston omniverse, a grounded-realm figure of the sixth era, only two ages old. Its influence is felt through whispered bargains and the quiet unraveling of promises made in the shadows of the mortal world.

rites.name: Pelustar
rites.text: Pelustar is a concept of the old hunting instinct that moves through the grassland pride and the reed-marsh stalkers alike, taught to every young hunter in Jorernaston. Its lessons are sung at the edge of the Grounded realm as a counterweight to the restless hunger of the wilds. Its hunts end where the land's own balance is restored.

rites.name: Krouzhak
rites.text: Krouzhak is a concept of Jorernaston, an idea that the Three Futures keep as a shelved outcome in the Library during the Holy Age of flame and temple orders. It is remembered mostly as a warning carried by the orders of the age, who debate whether it describes a path already taken.

rites.name: Vesezasha
rites.text: Vesezasha is a concept in Jorernaston, a notion that appears when the ending of the world branches and the Library catalogs each outcome. It took its shape during the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between villages and the valleys that fed them. Its stories are told in the Three Futures as a warning about what is lost when a people cannot reach across their divisions.
